name: Steel Dynamics, Inc.

profile.description: Steel Dynamics is one of the largest U.S. steel producers and metals recyclers, operating electric-arc-furnace (EAF) flat-rolled and long-product mills, OmniSource metals recycling, New Millennium joist and deck fabrication, and a new recycled-aluminum flat-rolled mill in Columbus, Mississippi. Founded in 1993 by Keith Busse and Mark Millett and headquartered in Fort Wayne, Indiana, it is known for a non-union, profit-sharing culture. Theresa Wagler becomes CEO on January 1, 2027, with Millett moving to Executive Chairman.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): SDI built the Sinton, Texas flat-roll EAF mill and is now ramping its Columbus, Mississippi recycled-aluminum flat-rolled mill, where all three cold mills are operating and the aluminum operating loss narrowed 21% to $26M in Q3 2026 [1][2]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI-powered products or quantified AI-driven savings were found [4]. Market Share (2/2): Q3 2026 delivered record steel shipments of 3.8M tons and fabrication shipments rose 18% sequentially, extending SDI's position as a top-three U.S. steelmaker and a leading joist and deck supplier [1][2]. Pipeline (2/2): The first aluminum CASH line is expected to ship finished automotive products before year-end 2026 and the second becomes operational early in Q1 2027 [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No material R&D disclosure; spending sits inside capex, consistent with steel peers [5].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): SDI's principles of 'safety, performance, innovation' and placing people first, alongside its aim to be the highest-quality, lowest-cost metals solutions company, are clear but largely competitive positioning [4][5]. Community Impact (1/2): The company has reported over $35M of charitable giving over a decade and recycles 99% of its mill scale and EAF dust, though recent dollar figures are not prominent [6]. Employee Retention (1/2): Co-founder Mark Millett has led since 1993 and is handing off to long-time CFO Theresa Wagler, and every team member shares in profits, though Glassdoor reviews note long hours for maintenance technicians [3][4]. Insider Buying (0/2): No net open-market insider buying was found in the last 12 months.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Dividend stock (forced from portfolios.json) on all ten metrics (total weight 12). D/E of 45.1% scores 1.0; ROE of 20.8% scores 1.0; revenue growth of 34.8% YoY scores 1.0; 5yr revenue CAGR of about 13.6% ($9.6B in 2020 to $18.2B in 2025) scores 1.0; Forward P/E of 11.53 scores 1.0; profit margin of 8.8% scores 0.44 [1][7]. Dividend metrics: payout ratio of 18.7% scores 1.0 (x1); 22 consecutive years paid (since 2004) scores 1.0 (x2); 13 consecutive years of growth scores 1.0 (x1); and 5yr dividend CAGR of about 14.9% ($1.00 in 2020 to $2.00 in 2025, with the 2026 quarterly rate at $0.53) scores 1.0 (x2) [7]. Weighted sum 11.44/12 = 9.5, giving a score of 10. Liquidity floor cleared: 1.08M avg shares x $246.80 = $265M daily dollar volume [7].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (9/9): Melting scrap into steel and rolling aluminum are physical processes AI cannot displace, and AI data center construction adds demand for SDI's joists, deck, and structural steel, part of why fabrication shipments rose 18% sequentially in Q3 2026 [1][2]. Reshoring and infrastructure spending add further non-AI demand. AI Opportunity (0/1): SDI does not report quantified revenue from AI-specific products or data-center customers, so the tiebreaker is not awarded [1].

infinite_game.summary: Sinek would see in SDI one of the rare industrials where culture is the strategy: Millett calls sustaining it 'sacrosanct', and profit sharing for every team member has held since 1993 [3]. Counter-cyclical greenfield bets (Sinton, then a $2.7B aluminum mill) show long-term thinking, and an internal CEO succession preserves continuity. Its competitive framing, built on being the lowest-cost producer, keeps it short of a fully infinite mindset.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): The people-first, profit-sharing cause has guided SDI for three decades and shapes behavior, but it is articulated mainly as a means to low-cost leadership rather than a vision of a better world [3][4].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (2/2): SDI built the Sinton flat-roll mill through the pandemic and committed about $2.7B to an aluminum mill in a market new to it, accepting startup losses (still $26M in Q3 2026) for long-term capability [1][2].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (2/2): A non-union, profit-sharing model, employee autonomy cited in 2026 Glassdoor reviews, and co-founder continuity with internal succession to Theresa Wagler create a strong Circle of Safety [3][4].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Expanding from steel into recycled aluminum and biocarbon is a significant adjacency, but SDI remains a metals producer, so it is evolution rather than reinvention [1][5].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): SDI defines itself as the lowest-cost, most profitable producer and benchmarks margins against Nucor and integrated mills, competitive language rather than learning from rivals [3].

investment_thesis: Steel Dynamics is in a strong upcycle: Q3 2026 net sales rose 35% to $6.5B, net income jumped 87% to $756M ($5.26/share), adjusted EBITDA reached $1.2B, and steel shipments set a record of 3.8M tons as the average external selling price rose $102 sequentially to $1,400/ton [1][2]. Steel operating income was $1.0B, cash flow from operations was $846M, and the aluminum mill narrowed its loss as all three cold mills came online [1]. With D/E of 45%, ROE of 21%, a forward P/E of 11.5, an 18.7% payout ratio, and 13 straight years of dividend growth, Infrastructure scores a full 10 [7].
thesis_continued: The bear case is cyclicality and execution. Steel prices and scrap spreads are at elevated, tariff-supported levels that could reverse with weaker demand or trade-policy changes, and trailing profit margin is only 8.8% [7]. The Columbus aluminum mill is still losing money ($26M in Q3), with coolant-related yield losses and a second CASH line not operational until early Q1 2027 [1]. The CEO transition from co-founder Millett to Theresa Wagler on January 1, 2027 tests the culture, and Sustainalytics rates ESG risk 'High' (31.4) because of steelmaking's emissions exposure [3][6].
key_catalysts: First aluminum CASH line shipping finished automotive sheet before year-end 2026 and the second line operating in early Q1 2027, moving aluminum toward profit [1]
Sustained record steel shipments and $1,400/ton average pricing supported by tariffs, reshoring, and data center construction [1][2]
Smooth CEO transition to Theresa Wagler on January 1, 2027 with continued capital returns [3]
key_risks: Steel price and metal-spread normalization if tariffs ease or construction and auto demand weaken [7]
Prolonged aluminum startup losses (Q3 2026 operating loss $26M) or yield problems at the $2.7B Columbus mill [1]
Leadership transition risk as co-founder Mark Millett steps back after more than three decades [3]
